pieces.title: The same hole twice
pieces.caption: A checker inside the system that made the error shares its hole: “the same blind spot signs off on itself”. A different mind has different holes. *What is real and what is a choice:* One slice repeated three times is my turn on the Swiss cheese model, which is about different layers that fail when their holes align. The right panel shows a catch; a different mind makes that likely, not certain, and the page calls its claim “a strongly-recurring pattern, not a proven law”. *Leaking in:* Latent Error, which holds the model: “Systems fail when these "holes" align across layers.” Named in the footer; its avatar is no longer drawn.

verdicts.file: No Mind Checks Itself — rich — the same hole twice.svg
verdicts.why: A good picture of the page's sentence, and "one layer drawn three times" is a real thought. Three fixes. (1) The honest line calls it "James Reason's Swiss cheese model". Reason's model is different defences whose holes sometimes line up; one mind's slice repeated three times is the maker's turn on it, and should be owned as that. (2) The right panel shows the error stopped for certain.

remade.file: No Mind Checks Itself — rich — the same hole twice.svg
remade.what: The honest line credited Reason's model for the maker's own turn on it, the right panel showed a certain catch, and its third slice was unlabelled with an avatar against it. The turn is owned, the right panel has two labelled slices and says likely, not certain, and the avatar is gone.
